clue.text: For the record, saint's after a spanner

indicators.note: the saint's name comes after the spanner in the answer

parts.note: an arch spans a gap, so it is a spanner in the bridging sense
St Ives (Ivo, Yves) is a saint, so the saint's name is Ives

explanation.surface: Someone explains for the record that a saint's name follows a spanner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A spanner' looks like a tool but is an arch, which spans a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Archives are the stored body of documents, collectively the official record of an institution.

clue.text: H, as with Hook?

parts.note: Captain Hook of Peter Pan is a pirate

explanation.surface: A question whether the letter H is said the way Captain Hook would say it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' is a link; Hook stands for what he is, a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoneticians call the letter H, the breathy sound, an aspirate.

clue.text: "12 across 17 down: _____?" (A homely whip would serve)

indicators.note: the letters would serve if put to use in a new order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A call-centre greeting, with a jokey aside about serving a homely whip.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the gap in the phrase completed by 12 across and 17 down: a call-centre worker named Tracy answering the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptionist who announces her name usually follows it with this standard polite offer of assistance.

clue.text: Guide protectors of head island

parts.note: helmets, or helms, protect the head
the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A guide to the head-protecting gear worn on some island.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmsman steers a vessel, so he guides it on its course.

clue.text: One in the pavilion makes 20 runs

parts.note: a score is twenty
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer sitting in the pavilion scores twenty runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the pavilion is the clubhouse; the official scorer sits there keeping the tally.
explanation.definitionFit: The scorer at a cricket match records the runs from a seat in or near the pavilion.

clue.text: Award for setter backing his own

indicators.note: backing means the setter's word is turned round to run backwards

parts.note: the crossword setter refers to himself as me
the setter's own possessive is my

explanation.surface: The crossword setter supports his own nomination for an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support but turns ME into EM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Emmy is the American television industry's annual prize statuette.

clue.text: For first option there's no end — keep going!

indicators.note: no end says the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: phone menus say press one for the first option

explanation.surface: An automated phone menu cheerfully urging the caller to persist.
explanation.walkthrough: Telephone menus say 'press one' for the first choice; dropping its last letter gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To press on is an idiom for continuing resolutely despite difficulty.

clue.text: … and thank you for calling … (If you are, don't mention it)

definitions.text: … and thank you for calling … (If you are, don't mention it)

parts.words: … and thank you for calling … (If you are, don't mention it)
parts.note: a call centre greets callers this way, and someone told they are this replies with the polite stock phrase don't mention it

explanation.surface: A call-centre script, with a dry aside about polite replies.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: the word that goes with 'thank you for calling' in a phone greeting, and the word in 'you're ___', which means 'don't mention it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Callers are told they are glad to be received, and 'you are welcome' answers thanks just like 'don't mention it'.

clue.text: Bond's said to be Asian

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken and we write what is heard

parts.note: a bond or link is a tie

explanation.surface: A claim that James Bond is reputedly Asian.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond looks like 007, but it is a tie, which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thai is a person from Thailand, a country in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Enjoy yourself with Kremer's problem in a month

indicators.note: in places the rearranged name inside the month

parts.note: May is a month

indicators.note: a problem with the name means its letters are jumbled

parts.note: the surname Kremer, taken as its letters

explanation.surface: Someone advised to enjoy themselves while working on Kremer's puzzle during a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem' looks like a puzzle Kremer has set, but it signals the jumble; the scrambled name sits inside the month.
explanation.definitionFit: To make merry is an idiom for celebrating and having fun.

clue.text: Thinker ran a pub: he might have been an actor

indicators.note: might have been says these letters could become something else when reorganised

explanation.surface: A philosopher who ran a pub could have been an actor instead.
explanation.walkthrough: All sixteen letters of THINKER RAN A PUB HE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Katharine Hepburn was a Hollywood star, a four-time Oscar winner on screen.

clue.text: See 25
South African with a bone but no drink

indicators.note: but no says letters are taken away from the phrase before

parts.note: the phrase is taken as its letters; once the drink's letters go, the rest happen to run together, a coincidence of the deletion rather than a hiding
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: A South African dog with a bone but nothing to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove W, I, N, E in order from WITHABONE to leave the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Thabo Mbeki, president of South Africa, is a well-known bearer of this first name.

clue.text: Scotsman takes a chance on a shrub

parts.note: Tam is a Scottish man's name, as in Tam o' Shanter
a risk is a chance taken

explanation.surface: A Scotsman gambles on a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The tamarisk is a feathery-leaved shrub of coasts and dry places.

clue.text: Follower, a female for the record

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A female follower identified for the record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For the record' is not an aside: EP is a kind of record.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep are proverbial followers, people who go along with the crowd.

clue.text: See 17
Labour starts in suffering reaching climax, when candour is needed

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word for suffering

parts.note: pains is suffering

indicators.note: starts picks the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: peaking means reaching a climax or high point

explanation.surface: The start of labour pains reaching their peak, a time for frank talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' suggests childbirth or the party; only its first letter L is used, inside PAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain speaking is frank, direct talk, which is what candour means.

clue.text: Drops the broken fragment

indicators.note: broken says the letters before it are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone drops a broken piece of pottery.
explanation.definitionFit: A potsherd is a fragment of broken pottery, found at archaeological sites.

clue.text: Old connection paid into source of power and energy

indicators.note: into puts the abbreviation inside the word for the power source

parts.note: steam powers engines
PD is an abbreviation for paid
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An old link paid into some source of power and energy.
explanation.walkthrough: PD goes into STEAM, giving STEPDAM, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepdame is an archaic word for a stepmother, a relation through marriage.

clue.text: See 16 across
Endlessly discuss races with one that's thrown over 2

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the next word is dropped

parts.note: to confer is to discuss
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone talks endlessly about races involving a thing tossed over a couple.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' here is a pair, a newly married couple, over whom paper scraps are thrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Confetti is the paper scraps thrown over a bride and groom at a wedding.

clue.text: Iron over 14 like Christmas pudding?

indicators.note: over means the iron symbol goes round the young animal

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
14 down is sheep, and a lamb is a young sheep

explanation.surface: Ironing over a sheep, as if it were a Christmas pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Christmas pudding, a British festive dessert, is traditionally doused in brandy and set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Flambé describes food covered in spirit and set alight, as a festive pudding traditionally is.

clue.text: See 3
It conceals expression of satisfaction arising from break in

indicators.note: conceals means the word It holds the other piece inside
arising in a down clue means reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a cat's purr expresses contentment

explanation.surface: Something hiding a contented sound arising from a break-in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arising' suits a down clue, where the word reads upwards; a cat's contented sound is the expression of satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst in or invade suddenly.

clue.text: To get a cleaner's job we enter in a sunsuit

indicators.note: enter means the pronoun goes inside the phrase before it

parts.note: to get a cleaner's job is to be a char, a British word for a cleaning lady

explanation.surface: Someone takes a cleaning job and shows up in a sunsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: A char is a British cleaning woman; WE goes into BE A CHAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Beachwear is clothing worn at the seaside, a sunsuit being one example.

clue.text: Grouse as food (not 14)

definitions.meaning: to grouse is to complain or gripe
meat that is not from sheep, the answer to 14, but from cattle

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like the game bird but is the verb to complain.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is slang for a grievance, and also the meat of cattle rather than sheep.

clue.text: Dagger heard to fold

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken and the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: a crease is a fold

explanation.surface: A dagger said to fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A kris is a Malay dagger with a wavy blade.

clue.text: See 1
See 11
West Yorkshire valley that can't lose lively actor

parts.note: the Spen Valley is in West Yorkshire
a cert is a certainty, a bet that cannot lose
racy means lively

explanation.surface: A lively actor from a Yorkshire valley who can't lose.
explanation.walkthrough: West Yorkshire is a county in northern England; the River Spen gives its valley the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Spencer Tracy was an Oscar-winning Hollywood film star.
